decisions.reason: The source defines connector and antenna placement for the later single integrated board, not the separate legacy main board.
The source applies to the integrated-board layout and does not revise the separate power-board mechanical layout.
The integrated-board edge constraints do not alter the mechanical layout of the separate sensor board.

Although both requirements mention J_BAT, the candidate describes the separate power-board battery interface; the source places J_BAT on the integrated board and does not revise the legacy interface state.
Grouping J_DISP_LED with the other display connectors is a mechanical-layout constraint and does not change the backlight circuit specification.
The source does not identify the light-sensor port or change its quantity, connector type, interface, or purpose.
The source concerns placement on the integrated board and does not change the separate main board's connector inventory or architecture.
The mechanical constraints operate within the already selected single-board architecture and do not change its consolidation or functionality-preservation requirements.
The ESP32 antenna orientation and keepout are mechanical and RF layout constraints; they do not change the breakout header pitch.
The source adds necessary placement constraints but does not revise the integrated board's cost, sourcing, connector-reduction, or functionality-preservation policy.
The source addresses connectors on the integrated board and does not modify the separate sensor board's connector inventory, pinouts, or count.
Battery-relative placement and antenna keepout do not change the power-management component, required rails, charging behavior, or battery-efficiency goal.
